The Future of Urban Living

Smaller footprints, shared spaces and softer streets: five ideas shaping how cities will feel in the next decade.

Written by

Mateo Alvarez

Published

Aug 22, 2026

Cities are getting denser, but density does not have to mean discomfort. The best new urban housing feels more like a village stacked vertically than a filing cabinet for people.

Shared is the new private

Roof gardens, workshops, laundries that double as cafés: generous shared rooms let apartments stay compact without life feeling small. Neighbours become a feature, not a side effect.

The city's most valuable amenity is not a gym. It is a place to run into someone you like.

— Mateo Alvarez, Principal Architect

Adapt, don't demolish

The greenest building is the one that already exists. Retrofitting, repurposing and adding lightly to existing structures will define the next generation of urban architecture.
